chapter: Family follow-ups from the first reels
title: Junior Philharmonic and conductor Henry Rothwell
summary: Royal as concert master at McKinley Junior High and the city Junior Philharmonic under Walter Henry Rothwell, who gave him free conducting lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: On the earlier tape, you mentioned playing with the Los Angeles Junior Philharmonic Orchestra and you weren't certain of the conductor's name. I think you have it now, right?
Yes, Henry Rothwell. (PHONETIC).
Didn't you find out it was Walter Henry Rothwell?
Yeah, well, all I knew was Henry.
I see, okay, (inaudible).

He also taught me -- he took a little liking to me. I think I was the only little black boy down there. So, he took a liking to me and had me to come down to his office, down to the Philharmonic, and he taught me a little bit about conducting and how it was supposed to be for free.
How did you happen -- since you say you were the only black boy down there, I mean, it must have been
unusual (inaudible).

Usually those type of things were city-wide participation and during the course of each semester, usually at one, two or three times during the year, the leading instrumentalists of all the orchestras throughout the city would be chosen, like one or two from each school, and when they were altogether, they composed what was called as the Junior Philharmonic Orchestra.
But you were really the outstanding music student --
I was the outstanding musician, yes, in my junior high school.
(Inaudible).
I went to McKinley Junior High School. It's now called Carver, after George Washington Carver. But I was what was called the concert master in the orchestra at that time.
So, how many years -- was it all during your junior high school (inaudible)?
Yeah, I went there for a couple of years. See, the junior high school only encompasses the seventh, eighth and ninth year, so it was probably around my eighth and ninth year that I went there.
And how often did the Junior Philharmonic perform?
Oh, maybe twice a year, for some special occasion.
And how often did you get together to play or rehearse?
If they were going to have a particular concert, well, then you have one or two rehearsals before the concert and that was all. That's all it encompassed.
But you had the conductor of the adult Philharmonic Orchestra working with you?
Yes.
(Inaudible) or something?
No, I know one of the years, he was the conductor.
Because I checked on him (inaudible) 1919 through 1927.
That's right. Well, that was during the time there, because I graduated from high school when I was 27 -- in 1927.
(Inaudible).
From junior high school, I graduated. Yes, junior high school, I graduated in '27, June.
That was (inaudible).
Right.
(Inaudible).
That's right.
